title: Postgres connection pool exhaustion after v2.3.0 Friday deploy
symptoms: payments-api p99 latency above 4.8s and checkout error rate above 23% starting ~12 minutes after the v2.3.0 Friday deploy; new checkouts failing with DB connection errors.
log_snippet:
2026-05-15T14:32:10Z ERROR payments-api [pool-2] org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
p99_latency=4820ms error_rate=23.4% deploy=v2.3.0 (12 min ago)
root_cause: The v2.3.0 deploy's new order-confirmation retry path opens a DB session per retry without releasing it on timeout, exhausting the 20-connection Postgres pool within minutes of Friday peak traffic.

fix_attempts.notes: rolled back to v2.2.9; pool exhaustion persisted, sessions already leaked before rollback took effect
raised max pool size from 20 to 60 and force-closed stale sessions

resolution: Pool size increase (20 -> 60) resolved the outage; the rollback was reverted afterward.
postmortem: Root cause (unreleased DB sessions on retry timeout in order-confirmation) is not yet fixed in code; pool resize is a workaround. Action item: add a session timeout and explicit release in order-confirmation retries -- not yet implemented.
